mcqs.question: Many students think that the principal focus of a convex lens lies on the same side as the object. Which statement correctly identifies the principal focus for a convex lens?

options.A: It is the point on the principal axis where parallel rays converge after refraction.
options.B: It is the point on the principal axis where parallel rays appear to diverge after refraction.
options.C: It is located at the optical centre of the lens.
options.D: It coincides with the centre of curvature of the lens surface.

mcqs.answer: It is the point on the principal axis where parallel rays converge after refraction.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex (converging) lens, parallel rays incident on the lens are refracted so that they meet at the principal focus on the side opposite the incoming light. Option A states this correctly. Option B describes the focus of a concave lens, C is the optical centre, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image of a distant tree on a screen placed 20 cm from the lens. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: When the object is at a very large distance, the image is formed at the focal plane; therefore the image distance equals the focal length. The screen is 20 cm away, so the focal length is 20 cm. Options A, C, and D are incorrect values.

mcqs.question: Which description correctly represents the ray diagram for a convex lens when the object is placed beyond twice the focal length (2F)?

options.A: A ray through the optical centre passes undeviated, a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the focal point on the opposite side, and a ray directed towards the focal point on the object side emerges parallel, forming a real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F.
options.B: A ray through the optical centre passes undeviated, a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the focal point on the same side, and a ray directed towards the focal point on the object side emerges through the centre, forming a virtual, upright, enlarged image beyond 2F.
options.C: All rays diverge after passing through the lens, producing a virtual, upright image at the optical centre.
options.D: Rays converge at the optical centre, producing a real, upright image at the principal focus.

mcqs.answer: A ray through the optical centre passes undeviated, a ray parallel to the principal axis refracts through the focal point on the opposite side, and a ray directed towards the focal point on the object side emerges parallel, forming a real, inverted, reduced image between F and 2F.
mcqs.explanation: For a convex lens with the object beyond 2F, the three principal rays behave as described in option A, giving a real, inverted image located between F and 2F. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect ray behaviours or image characteristics for this situation.

mcqs.question: A convex lens of focal length 12 cm is used to form an image of a candle placed 18 cm from the lens. What is the nature and position of the image?

options.A: Real, inverted, 36 cm on the opposite side of the lens
options.B: Real, inverted, 27 cm on the opposite side of the lens
options.C: Virtual, upright, 36 cm on the same side of the lens
options.D: Virtual, upright, 27 cm on the same side of the lens

mcqs.answer: Real, inverted, 36 cm on the opposite side of the lens
mcqs.explanation: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v + 1/u (sign convention: u = -18 cm, f = +12 cm), we get 1/v = 1/12 - 1/18 = 1/36, so v = +36 cm. Positive v indicates a real image on the opposite side, and images formed by convex lenses are inverted. Hence option A is correct; the other options misstate the image type or distance.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a convex lens from a concave lens?

options.A: A convex lens converges parallel rays; a concave lens diverges them.
options.B: A convex lens diverges parallel rays; a concave lens converges them.

mcqs.answer: A convex lens converges parallel rays; a concave lens diverges them.
mcqs.explanation: Convex (converging) lenses bring parallel incident rays to a focus, while concave (diverging) lenses cause parallel rays to spread out as if originating from a focal point. Option A states this distinction correctly; the other options reverse or ignore the behavior.

mcqs.question: The optical centre of a thin lens is the point where:

options.A: The principal axis meets the lens surface
options.B: Any incident ray passes through without deviation
options.C: The focal length is measured from

mcqs.answer: Any incident ray passes through without deviation
mcqs.explanation: For a thin lens, the optical centre is the geometric centre; a ray passing through this point experiences no net deviation because the angles of incidence on the two surfaces cancel. Options A, C, and D describe other lens features, not the optical centre.

mcqs.question: The principal focus of a convex lens is defined as:

options.A: The point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis converge after refraction
options.B: The point where rays appear to diverge after refraction
options.D: The point where the lens is thickest

mcqs.answer: The point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis converge after refraction
mcqs.explanation: In a convex (converging) lens, parallel rays are refracted to meet at the principal focus on the side opposite the incoming light. Option A captures this definition. Option B describes the focus of a concave lens, while C and D are unrelated.

mcqs.question: A convex lens forms a real image of a distant street lamp on a screen placed 15 cm behind the lens. What is the focal length of the lens?
mcqs.explanation: For a distant object, the image is formed at the focal plane, so the image distance equals the focal length. The screen is 15 cm from the lens, therefore the focal length is 15 cm. Options A, B, and D are incorrect distances.
